title: Chart accessibility and rendering performance: virtualized line rendering & ARIA semantics
creator: Avery Patel
description:
Problem: Time-series charts in the Design System render slowly when fed high-cardinality series (50+ lines) and suffer from accessibility gaps: screen readers read unhelpful SVG path data, legend keyboard focus is inconsistent, and tooltips are not exposed to assistive tech.

Goal: Deliver a design + engineering approach that: 1) improves rendering performance for large-series charts to meet interactive SLOs on typical client devices, and 2) makes chart elements (series, legend items, tooltips) usable with screen readers and keyboard-only interaction. All changes should be style-token-driven and backward-compatible with existing chart props.

Scope: Design tokens (color/opacity/line-width), legend & tooltip UX, ARIA patterns for complex charts, and a recommended rendering strategy (virtualized canvas layer + SVG accessibility layer or optimized SVG using path simplification). Not in scope: implementing server-side downsampling or new chart types (sparklines are out of scope for this ticket).

Success metrics (acceptance criteria):
- Rendering: Large charts (50 series x 1000 points) render at >30 fps on mid-range laptops when panning/zooming in our internal perf harness.
- Accessibility: Screen reader reads a concise summary for the chart and allows linearized navigation of series and legend items with meaningful labels (NVDA/VoiceOver tested).
- Keyboard: Legend items are reachable via Tab and togglable with Space/Enter; focused legend item indicates series visibility in the visual view.
- Developer experience: New token usages documented and storybook stories added for interactive, high-cardinality scenarios.

Design notes / Proposed approach: 
1) Rendering strategy: Recommend layered approach: a lightweight canvas renderer for bulk path drawing + a minimal SVG layer for interactive hit targets and focusable elements. Canvas handles continuous drawing (fast), SVG provides semantic elements for screen readers and keyboard interactions. Where canvas-only is unavoidable, generate an off-DOM lightweight accessibility tree (aria-hidden=false nodes) that mirrors legend/series metadata.

2) Virtualization & simplification: Use incremental path drawing + Douglas-Peucker simplification for long series during pan/zoom, and coarse downsampling for overview mode. Provide a chart prop to control simplification tolerance tuned via token (e.g., token: chart.simplify.tolerance).

3) ARIA patterns: Chart root gets role="region" and an aria-labelledby pointing to a visible chart title. Provide aria-describedby linking to a short textual summary (e.g., "7 series, last 30 days, primary metric: latency"). Series are represented in the accessibility tree as a list (role="list") with listitems (role="listitem") and each item exposes name, current latest value, and visibility toggle instructions. Legend items are real buttons with aria-pressed reflecting visibility. Tooltips expose role="status" or a live region with polite updates when keyboard focus moves between points.

4) Tokens & theming: Add tokens for high-contrast stroke colors (chart.color.high-contrast.*), disabled opacity (chart.opacity.disabled), focus ring (chart.focus.width, chart.focus.color), and simplified stroke widths for dense modes. Ensure tokens align with existing token naming conventions and are documented in the token registry.

5) Performance fallbacks: When device capability is low or browser memory is constrained, fallback to precomputed downsampled series and show a toast / console hint for developers. Autoswitch based on heuristics (device memory, frame time).

6) UX edge cases: For charts with >100 series, move to an 'overview mode' by default that collapses visual stroke detail and forces legend pagination/search. Legend search should be keyboard-accessible and offer a matching highlight without forcing re-renders of all paths.

Deliverables: 
- Figma flows for keyboard/voiceover navigation and legend pagination (links below).
- Storybook stories: "Chart / High cardinality / Accessibility" and "Chart / Performance / Canvas+SVG".
- Design token PR and updated token documentation.
- Implementation checklist and QA matrix for screen reader testing.

comments: 2025-02-18 Avery Patel: Initial triage — mapped problem space with Eng (Riley) and PM. Decided to prioritize canvas+SVG hybrid to balance perf and semantics.
2025-02-20 Riley Thompson (Eng): Ran quick prototype using canvas draw + offscreen SVG for hit targets. Early numbers show 2.3x improvement on a 2019 MacBook Pro for 40 series.
2025-02-22 Morgan Chen (Design): Updated Figma flows to show keyboard focus states and added token suggestions for focus ring and disabled opacity.
2025-02-24 Accessibility review (external consultant): Recommended explicit live region use for tooltip announcements and avoiding aria-hidden on elements that convey essential data.
2025-02-26 Morgan Chen: Pushing design tokens PR and storybook scaffolding. Added acceptance criteria checklist. Assigned follow-up to ENG-2603 for implementation spike.
activity: Decision: Use canvas for bulk rendering + SVG for interactive/accessibility layer (favored over pure SVG due to perf tests).
Trade-off: Canvas improves perf but requires a mirrored accessibility tree; we will implement a small, memory-efficient list representation for screen readers.
Follow-up: ENG-2603 (spike) to prototype hit-testing strategy; PM assigned to ENG-2603 for scope alignment.

Review feedback: PM wants toggling performance to be near-instant (<100ms) for legend interactions; engineer proposed debounce-free visibility toggles using CSS opacity for SVG layer and GPU-accelerated compositing for canvas layer.
Approval: Design lead signed off on tokens and Figma flows on 2025-02-25.
notes_for_engineering: Include a small, declarative accessibility API for the chart component (props: a11yTitle, a11ySummary, legendAriaLabel). Default behavior must not regress existing apps. Provide a migration guide and storybook examples.
qa_checks: Screen reader: NVDA (Windows) and VoiceOver (macOS) pass for chart summary and series navigation.
Keyboard: Tab order to legend, enter/space toggles, arrow keys navigate legend list.
Perf: 50 series x 1000 pts renders >30fps for pan/zoom in perf harness.
Tokenization: New tokens surfaced in token registry and available in theme switcher.
Regression: Existing chart stories unaffected visually on default data.
